doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Day-to-day management, agent and touring with her son
summary: She and husband Rick work with manager and agent on bookings, and son Jack travels with them.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Do you see figures on on-line sales? I mean does the record company provide you with that kind of information if you want it?

If I wanted them absolutely, yeah. I mean I’ve looked at that stuff before. Most of the time I don’t really. I focus on my end of the job, which is putting on a really good show, maintaining a healthy instrument, and just being involved in all the day to day little things. You know, do you want to take this gig or do you want this tour to run this way or do you want to be on a bill with this person or do this special event or this charity event, all that kind of stuff I’m handling every day and being involved with, as well as my husband, who has a huge role in all of that stuff.
You’re a team in that. And do you have an agent?
And you correspond with the agent, and the agent may call you up and say look do you want to go to Ft. Lauderdale, they’re offering this — I mean do you get into that nitty gritty?

Yeah. I do that with my manager, and we do that with pretty much every show. You know everything is run by me and we figure everything out together, which is great. Especially now because I have a 2-year-old that travels with us, and it’ll be the kind of thing like well you know there might not be money for Jack’s plane ticket on this trip do you still want to take it, but if we connect it to this gig then it will work out and can your parents watch him during that time. You know, it’s like those kind of details. Because Jack comes with us everywhere.

The only time he doesn’t come on the road is if it’s someplace that might be a little dangerous for him or something like last month I went to Palermo for one day — well it was for a couple of days but it was for one gig — so I wasn’t going to subject him to the time change. But yeah I’m involved in that kind of stuff every day with the management. The agent calls the manager, the manager calls me, and we do everything and then she goes back to the agent and he books. You know it’s that kind of thing.
